subject: Reliability qualification recap & next steps — AuroraBank
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maya Patel <maya.patel@aurorabank.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Feb 2027 15:05:00 -0800
Subject: Reliability qualification recap & next steps — AuroraBank

Hi Maya —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our side so we have alignment and clear next steps. Please correct anything I get wrong.

Summary of pain and goals:
- Recent multi-hour incident in December that impacted transactional verification flows; primary symptom was degraded model responsiveness under burst load.
- Goal: move to a platform that guarantees predictable tail latency for customer-facing prompts (target: p95 < 120ms for short prompts, p95 < 300ms for longer multi-turn flows) and a clear graceful degradation story so core flows fail into a safe path (cached/KV or smaller model) rather than timing out.
- Security/compliance: AuroraBank needs KMS integration and audit logs for model I/O.

Current stack you shared:
- Frontend: internal service that calls a third-party managed API for text generation.
- Sensitive flows: on-prem preprocessing and tokenization; model requests currently go to cloud vendor endpoints (no private-hosted inference).
- Observability: basic metrics + vendor-provided dashboards; lack of request-level tracing across retries/fallbacks.

Success criteria (what would make this a win for AuroraBank):
1) Clear SLOs for latency and availability with documented fallback behaviors.
2) Private control plane / VPC option or dedicated capacity for regulated customer data.
3) Integration plan for KMS and audit log exports.
4) Proof-of-concept demonstrating graceful degradation under load within 4 weeks.

Proposed next steps (from Redwood):
- I attached a short mutual action plan (MAP-AuroraBank-Outline.pdf) that breaks down milestones and owners.
- Security snapshot (attached) with initial answers — we can expand into your vendor questionnaire.
- Technical deep dive with our infra lead (Neha) to walk through fallback strategies (model variants, region failover, prefix caching) — can we do that Tue or Wed morning PST?
- We’ll sketch an SLO matrix and propose a Dedicated capacity trial for the most critical flows.

Attachments: [Attachment: MAP-AuroraBank-Outline.pdf (PDF)], [Attachment: security-snapshot-aurorabank.json (JSON)]

Open questions for you before the deep dive:
- Which flows are highest priority for availability vs cost tradeoffs (transaction verification vs personalization)?
- Any constraints on cross-region data transfer or required region residency?
- Who on procurement should we loop in to get a preliminary procurement timeline?

Thanks — I’ll follow up with a calendar invite once you confirm availability.

— Jordan
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com
Phone: +1 415-555-0187

From: Maya Patel <maya.patel@aurorabank.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Reliability qualification recap & next steps — AuroraBank

Jordan — thanks for the clear write-up. This matches our internal notes. A couple quick answers:
- Priority: transaction verification (high) > onboarding personalization (medium).
- Region residency: production data must remain in us-east-1; we can accept multi-region read-replicas for caches but no writes outside the US.
- Procurement: looping in ryan.chu@aurorabank.com (cc'd below) — he’ll own timelines and contract questions.

I can do Tue 16 Feb at 10:00am PST for the technical deep dive. Please include Neha and any infra docs you want us to review ahead of time.

Maya Patel
Head of Platform Engineering, AuroraBank
maya.patel@aurorabank.com

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maya Patel <maya.patel@aurorabank.com>, Ryan Chu <ryan.chu@aurorabank.com>, procurement@aurorabank.com
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Reliability qualification recap & next steps — AuroraBank

Great — I’ve booked Tue 16 Feb 10:00am PST for the technical deep dive (calendar invite sent). Agenda (30–45m):
- Quick recap of incident profile you shared (5m)
- Redwood’s graceful degradation patterns: cached responses, small-model fallback, regional failover, and circuit-breaker strategies (15m)
- Integration checklist: KMS/HSM options, audit log exports, VPC/Dedicated capacity (10m)
- Open Q&A and trial outline (10m)

Neha — can you prepare a short SLO matrix and a strawman fallback plan we can present? Aditya — can you pull a sample cost estimate for a 4-week Dedicated trial scoped to transaction verification flows?

Attachments: [Attachment: MAP-AuroraBank-Outline.pdf (PDF)]

— Jordan

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Maya Patel <maya.patel@aurorabank.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Feb 2027 08:48:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Reliability qualification recap & next steps — AuroraBank

Thanks — I prepared an initial SLO matrix and fallback options for the call. High-level notes below and I’ll share slides during the deep dive.

SLO strawman for transaction verification (we can tune):
- Availability: 99.95% monthly (with defined maintenance windows)
- Latency targets: p50 < 80ms, p95 < 120ms for short prompts (<= 64 tokens); p95 < 300ms for longer flows.
- Fallbacks: primary -> warmed smaller model (quantized) -> cached KV result -> synchronous database fallback (3s timeout guard).

Region strategy:
- Primary: us-east-1 dedicated pool; cold standby in us-west-2 for failover with async replication of caches.

I’ll bring the SLO matrix and an example request flow visual.

— Neha
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com
